intro: Find your optimal daily protein intake based on your body weight, activity level and fitness goal — whether you want to lose fat, maintain or build muscle.

result.tip: Spread your protein across 3–5 meals for optimal muscle protein synthesis.

formula.title: How Protein Is Calculated
formula.explanation: Protein recommendations are expressed in grams per kilogram of body weight. Ranges are based on ISSN (International Society of Sports Nutrition) guidelines: 1.4–2.0 g/kg for active individuals, up to 2.2 g/kg for muscle gain.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: How much protein do I need per day?
faq.a1: The RDA is 0.8 g/kg, but for active adults and those seeking body composition changes, 1.4–2.2 g/kg is recommended by leading sports nutrition bodies.
faq.q2: Can I eat too much protein?
faq.a2: For healthy adults, high protein intakes up to 2.2 g/kg are well-tolerated. Extremely high intakes are rarely beneficial and may displace other nutrients. Those with kidney disease should consult their doctor.
faq.q3: What are the best protein sources?
faq.a3: High-quality sources include lean meats, fish, eggs, dairy (Greek yogurt, cottage cheese), legumes and, if needed, protein supplements. Aim for a variety of sources.
faq.a4: Distributing protein intake across meals (every 3–4 hours) supports muscle protein synthesis better than consuming it all at once. A pre-sleep protein dose (casein) can also be beneficial.
faq.q5: Is plant protein as effective as animal protein?
faq.a5: Plant proteins can be equally effective when total intake is adequate and a variety of sources are consumed. Combining legumes, grains and soy provides a complete amino acid profile.
